paragraphs: Evidence Grade supplies recordable media for storing evidence, including optical discs, USB cards and solid-state drives. The buyers it names are government agencies, prosecutors, district attorneys, courts, and law enforcement organizations at the state, local and county level. Those buyers, the company says, need media that stays readable until after the last appeal.

Different grades are matched to different storage conditions. A second grade is intended for semi-controlled conditions that are easier on the disc. Discs can carry human and machine-readable serialization meant to support chain of evidence procedures. The company describes inspection at intake and during manufacturing, with anything non-compliant thrown out.

The company says it has supplied this media to the law enforcement community since 2009. It states that its testing is meant to keep media readable for at least thirty-two years under adverse and semi-controlled conditions. It also describes itself as the sole source of several branded grades of optical media.

quote.text: These organizations require that any media used for original or derived evidence must be readable until after the last appeal.
